claims.text: THE WING HISTORY DID NOT RECORD IT AND THE WING HISTORIAN SAID SO IN WRITING. SSgt Paul J. Cahill, 379th Bombardment Wing historian, Research Record of Events, 17 January 1979: 'Following that request, I checked the Oct-Dec 75 Wing History and found no references to the incident.'

Capt. Myron Taylor's Memo for the Record of 18 January 1979 to SSgt Cahill gives the KC-135 crew's account and names the crew. Taylor: 'We followed the lights north out over Lake Huron and then the UFO swung south still over the lake toward the Saginaw Bay area of Michigan.' He records flashing lights similar to strobes flashing irregularly, two objects, and a separation speed estimated at about 1,000 knots.

The NORAD Senior Director's Log for 31 October 1975 records: 'Alerted by NCOC of a helicopter sighted over Wurtsmith AFB Wpns storage area, a tanker sighted same and pursued it 35 SE over Lake Huron.'

An Air Force Intelligence Service Alert Officer's Log entry of 31 October 1975 records: 'Contacted DIA OPS center and informed them of unidentified flight activity over two SAC bases near Canadian border.'

desc: The second episode of the 1975 sequence, and the one whose documentary afterlife is more instructive than the event. On the night of 30 October 1975 base personnel at Wurtsmith AFB saw the running lights of a low-flying craft that hovered and moved erratically near the perimeter; security police at the back gate reported an unlit helicopter coming over the gate and hovering at low altitude; a KC-135 tanker aloft was vectored onto it and pursued it out over Lake Huron. The NORAD Command Director's Log records the incident at 0355Z on 31 October 1975 and the Senior Director's Log records the tanker pursuing it thirty-five miles southeast over the lake. What makes this node matter beyond its own facts is what happened in January 1979: the 379th Bombardment Wing historian went looking for the incident in his own wing history, found no reference to it, and wrote that down, and the day after, the KC-135 instructor navigator wrote him a memorandum giving the crew's account. The board should treat that pair of documents as a standing caution about arguments from a unit history's silence.

timeline.text: The NORAD Senior Director's Log for 31 October 1975 records: 'Alerted by NCOC of a helicopter sighted over Wurtsmith AFB Wpns storage area, a tanker sighted same and pursued it 35 SE over Lake Huron.' A Joint Chiefs of Staff operational report of 30 October 1975 records that the Michigan Department of Natural Resources was contacted about aircraft searching for hunters spotting deer, and the explanation did not fit.
